2608.22725.title: SEAM: Shot Entity-Attribute Memory for Consistent Short-Drama Generation at Scale
2608.22725.paper_summary: Short-drama generation has grown into a large, industrialized pipeline, and as it scales from isolated shots to the episode level, visual continuity has become a critical bottleneck. Current agent frameworks generate each shot in isolation, so context drifts across shots and props, character posture, and blocking turn inconsistent. Once assembled, these small discrepancies amplify into severe visual breaks. We present SEAM (Shot Entity-Attribute Memory), a training-free, model-agnostic memory graph that repairs continuity entirely at the prompt-text layer by extracting a multi-dimensional state for every shot, retrieving only causally prior context over the resulting graph, filtering it selectively, and injecting the surviving constraints by natural-language prompt rewriting. We further release SEAM-Bench, a double-blind continuity storyboarding benchmark, on which SEAM raises cross-episode continuity recall from 0.700 to 0.946, generalizes across six mainstream text models, and yields consistent, though not yet significant, gains at the generated-image layer. Deployed as a mandatory stage in CreativeFitting's SEAM-Agent production pipeline over 201 shots, SEAM reaches a 96.5% director-acceptance rate with zero unsafe injections; a conservative counterfactual attributes at least 21.9 percentage points of that rate to its cross-episode memory.
2608.22725.paper_summary_zh: 短劇生成已經發展成為一個大型的工業化流程，隨著其從孤立的鏡頭擴展到集數層面，視覺連貫性已成為一個關鍵的瓶頸。當前的代理框架在孤立的情況下生成每個鏡頭，因此上下文在鏡頭之間漂移，道具、角色姿勢和場面調度變得不一致。一旦組裝完成，這些小的差異會放大成為嚴重的視覺斷裂。我們提出了 SEAM（鏡頭實體-屬性記憶），這是一個無需訓練的、模型無關的記憶圖，通過為每個鏡頭提取多維狀態，在提示文本層完全修復連貫性，僅檢索結果圖上的因果前置上下文，並有選擇性地過濾，通過自然語言提示重寫注入剩餘的約束。我們進一步發布了 SEAM-Bench，一個雙盲的連貫性故事板基準，在該基準上，SEAM 將跨集數的連貫性回憶從 0.700 提高到 0.946，並在六個主流文本模型中實現了泛化，雖然在生成圖層上尚未顯著，但仍然產生了一致的增益。作為 CreativeFitting 的 SEAM-Agent 生產流程中一個必須的階段，SEAM 在 201 個鏡頭上達到了 96.5% 的導演接受率，且沒有不安全的注入；一個保守的反事實將至少 21.9 個百分點的該比率歸因於其跨集數記憶。
